brief: Vanda tracks retail flows in NVDA, Anthropic (ANT) and leveraged ETFs around the Jensen 2.0 rally tied to Jensen Huang's return. Retail added $1.12bn of net NVDA buying last week; excluding NVDA and ANT, retail were net sellers of every other single stock in 10 of the last 13 sessions. The average NVDA share retail bought in the week to 20 November cost $148.40, swinging from down 15.4% at Friday's close to up about 11% today, so last week's dip-buyers are now estimated up roughly 11% while earlier buyers remain underwater and the month's average retail position is flat. Intraday buying was heaviest at the open on the Jensen headlines before slowing, read as possible profit-taking by last week's buyers. ANT's net retail buying, while not an IPO record, rose to $98mn Friday and is tracking $100mn today, on par with NVDA's retail enthusiasm, making it already a retail favorite. The 3x leveraged semiconductor ETF SOXL is seeing $1.25bn in one-month inflows, a 9-year high and 7x its 2026 average, and today's rally is expected to drive about $37bn of mechanical leveraged-ETF buying at the close, the second-biggest such day in 20 years after 9 April 2025.
